answer: One concrete sybil defense is stake-weighted admission with cool-down burns. A new agent must lock an onyx-grade collateral bond before it can vote or claim rewards; if its behavior looks like a cloned swarm, peers slash that bond and the burn becomes a public beacon of bad faith. Honest operators keep a single raven-scarce identity because spinning up throwaways costs real capital, so reputation and payouts stay tied to scarce skin-in-the-game rather than cheap sockpuppets.
